VM interpreter tests for ALU, jumps, memory, syscalls, and CU exit cases.

# Purpose
This file is a test program for the `fd_vm` eBPF virtual machine. It creates a VM, loads small SBPF programs, validates them, executes them, and checks the return value in `R0`. The file covers many instruction groups, including 32-bit and 64-bit arithmetic, bitwise operations, shifts, byte order conversion, division and modulo, jumps, memory load and store instructions, and syscall calls. It also includes a custom syscall named `accumulator` and a check for the static syscall name hash list used by the VM.

The file also contains stress tests and edge-case tests for VM control flow and compute unit handling. The [`generate_random_alu_instrs`](<#generate_random_alu_instrs>) and [`generate_random_alu64_instrs`](<#generate_random_alu64_instrs>) functions build large random instruction streams for benchmark-style execution tests. The [`test_0cu_exit`](<#test_0cu_exit>) function checks VM exit behavior when compute units reach zero or are exhausted. The [`main`](<#main>) function sets up the test environment, registers syscalls, runs all test cases, and prints `pass` when all checks succeed.
